doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Winning the Metronome contest with the L.A. City College band
summary: The City College band won the Metronome college contest and recorded four sides for Capitol on 78s.

bands.name: Los Angeles City College Jazz Band

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: No the first recording I ever did was 1953 with the L.A. City College Jazz Band. We’d just won the Metronome — remember that magazine?
You probably don’t remember it but I know you’ve heard of it.

They had a contest for the best college jazz dance band, and we won it. Sometimes I’m not sure why because Dave Baker, who has since become a very close friend of mine, his band was in it from Indiana and it was a wonderful band. Ours was more like a prom night band compared to that, but we did win it. We recorded four sides for Capitol records. They used to call them “sides” in those days.
They weren’t — well LPs — so you had how many, a total of eight songs or something?
No four. No these weren’t even LPs. These were 78s.
Actually it amounted to two 78s, one tune on each side.
Yes, that’s right, that’s it exactly.
Were you guys playing like really high powered Kenton-type arrangements at that point? © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
